target: Route "monotone-lemma" (mono): readout systems, thm:mono-iff, prop:mono-m3, prop:mono-translate, thm:mono-kbound, prop:mono-count, and the B^2 search — audited for novelty and significance against /data/ssg-proof/frontier.tex at HEAD 9f5a4d7.

findings.result_name: B^2 at m = 5 (the smallest open instance) / rem:mono-gap / the headline
findings.defect: STALE AND SUPERSEDED. The route's central open question — "is B^2 realised by a readout system of order (5,r)?" — is answered affirmatively in frontier.tex at HEAD. prop:b2-realised (commit e90d01b, integrated 02:55 while this route was still running) exhibits a nondegenerate stopping SSG on 138 vertices, FIVE Max and ONE Min, whose improvement outmap is exactly the 32-tuple the route calls B^2, verified from the game. One Min vertex means order (5,2) in the route's own language. The paper's summary (frontier.tex:199-200, 11709-11710) already reads "the third level is the smallest open instance". So the route's title ("tested at the smallest open size"), its headline, and rem:mono-gap as written are all false at HEAD. This is concurrency, not error — but the section must not be integrated in this framing. One salvageable fact: thm:mono-kbound gives k >= log2 chi_HK(B^2) = 1, and prop:b2-realised attains k = 1, so this is the single instance where that bound is sharp; that sentence is worth keeping and the rest of the subsection is not.

NOT NEW, AND STRICTLY WEAKER THAN WHAT IS ALREADY IN THE PAPER. thm:peak-law (frontier.tex:3478) says: for stopping G and any sigma, sigma' with val_{sigma'} >= val_sigma and unequal, the argmax A of phi = val_{sigma'} - val_sigma meets Delta(sigma,sigma'). Apply it with sigma' = sigma[u] for u in S_sigma (lem:switch gives the strict increase): Delta = {u}, hence u is in A, hence d(u) = max_V d. That is strictly stronger than "d(v) <= max_{w != v} d(w) for v != u" — the peak law says u is ALWAYS a maximiser, the route says only that no other vertex is the unique one — and it needs neither concavity nor |p|_1 <= 1, and it bounds over all of V, not just Vmax. cor:peak-sharp sharpens it further. The route's own remark (rem:mono-switchmax) reaches for thm:impedance, which is the wrong ancestor; the right one is thm:peak-law. Its 708-switch "verification" is a consistency check on a corollary of a theorem the paper proves. Do not integrate.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex:3478-3520 (thm:peak-law), 3521-3546 (cor:peak-sharp), 2909-2930 (lem:switch). thm:peak-law was integrated at 03:00 (commit 9f5a4d7) and the route's last file is timestamped 02:53, so this is concurrent duplication, not appropriation.

findings.defect: ALREADY ASSERTED IN THE PAPER, AND AN UNLABELLED REDISCOVERY OF PUBLISHED WORK. rem:gsharp-bigcube (frontier.tex:4367-4383) already states the general claim in almost the route's words — "every improvement orientation of a stopping SSG with Min vertices is the sink projection of a Holt-Klee unique sink orientation of a larger cube" — and, unlike the route, attributes it: "the unique sink orientation that the linear complementarity formulation of a stopping game induces on its cube of complementary bases, after Stickney and Watson, and that such orientations are Holt-Klee is the theorem of Gaertner, Morris and Ruest". Both Stickney-Watson and Gaertner-Morris-Ruest are on this project's standing rediscovery list, as is Hansen & Ibsen-Jensen's 2TBSG -> P-matrix LCP, which is the missing step. The route carries no attribution at all. Its added value is genuine but small: a direct SSG-internal proof (via freezing to a subgame and thm:contraction) of a statement the paper currently asserts on the strength of one computed instance. Integrate only as a one-paragraph proof folded into rem:gsharp-bigcube, keeping that remark's existing attribution — never as a new numbered proposition presented as new.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex:4367-4383 (rem:gsharp-bigcube); prior-art list in the round brief: "Stickney-Watson (LCP/USO correspondence)", "Gaertner-Morris-Ruest", "Hansen & Ibsen-Jensen (2TBSG -> P-matrix LCP)".

findings.result_name: Coverage measurement at m = 4 (rem:mono-cover4, the "44 non-Holt-Klee classes at r = 2")
findings.defect: FLOATING POINT ONLY — the one headline number here is unsupported at this project's evidentiary standard. t_cover4b.py calls sample.orientation, which is pure numpy: sample.fixed_point does np.linalg.solve with a 1e-14 switching threshold and a silent 60-iteration cap that returns an unconverged x without complaint, and sample.orientation accepts an orientation whenever a float margin exceeds tol = 1e-9. No hit is recomputed in Fractions, no game is built from any hit, and the logs record only counts. sample.py's own docstring claims "every hit is a realisation (re-verified exactly)" — that is false of the code as run. The r = 1 half is only a consistency check against prop:oneplayer-lp; the r = 2 half is the new claim ("a single Min vertex per readout already buys forty-four orientations that no one-player game can produce") and it rests on nothing exact. Either re-verify a handful of the 44 through t_exact.py/build.py (cheap — the seed and iteration index are recorded) or delete the claim. Rule 2 violation.
findings.evidence: monotone-lemma/sample.py lines 17-70 (numpy throughout, tol=1e-9, iters=60 with silent fallthrough); t_cover4b.py lines 60-84 (no exact recheck, only orbit lookup); cover4b_r2.log. Contrast t_verify3.py and t_vertrans.py, which DO build the game and check T_sigma(cand)=cand exactly — those results stand.

findings.defect: THREE DEFECTS, ONE OF THEM REPAIRABLE AND WORTH REPAIRING. (i) NOT AN IFF AS STATED: part (a) delivers a readout system that need be neither dyadic nor delta-leaky (a Max action pointing straight at another Max vertex gives a row with |p|_1 = 1, q = 0), while part (b) requires both. The round trip needs a rounding lemma — "every readout system arising from a stopping game can be shrunk and rounded to a dyadic delta-leaky one with the same outmap" — which the route proves only in the ONE-PLAYER case (lem:mono-perturb). As written the two halves do not compose, so the slogan "realisability IS concave interpolation" is not yet a theorem. (ii) NOT NEW IN ITS ONE-PLAYER HALF, AND UNCITED IN ITS TWO-PLAYER HALF'S ANCESTRY: rem:auso-census (frontier.tex:4156-4159) already says in so many words that "the right [space] is the normal form of lem:transport-dim's harmonic reduction, in which a one-player game is a family of 2m substochastic affine maps and the orientation is read off an arrangement", and prop:oneplayer-lp defines exactly the route's (p^{v,a}, q^{v,a}) as "the first-passage law of action a at v onto Vmax and onto t1". The theorem is also, essentially verbatim, round 12's UNVERIFIED item (v4) ("an exact two-way dictionary between stopping SSGs and 2|C| substochastic affine maps ... realisability of a prescribed AUSO is then an exact LP feasibility question"). Proving (v4) is a real contribution; not naming it is a labelling defect. (iii) SIZE-BLIND, WHICH IS THE ONLY PARAMETER THAT MATTERS: prop:auso-size and rem:auso-size have already ruled that realisability with m Max vertices and unbounded N is not the pivot's question — "What does obstruct the census, and cannot be searched away, is size." The repair is available and missing: build.py's Knuth-Yao chain uses at most D per set bit and at most (#targets) live slots per level, so part (b) actually produces N = O(m r D (m+k)) for denominator 2^D, i.e. the SUFFICIENT direction is size-faithful. The necessary direction is NOT (r <= 2^k is exponential in k), and the route never says so. State both and thm:mono-iff becomes a usable reformulation of rem:blowup-realise; leave them out and it is a restatement of the wrong question.
findings.evidence: mono.tex:120-170 (def:mono-system, thm:mono-iff); frontier.tex:4156-4159 (rem:auso-census), 4264-4270 (prop:oneplayer-lp), 4166-4200 (prop:auso-size, rem:auso-size); monotone-lemma/build.py:1-52 (the DDG chain, n_j bounded by the number of live targets).

findings.defect: THE COUNTING HALF IS prop:auso-size (the route says so — good), THE NEW HALF IS WEAKER THAN TRIVIAL, AND ONE STEP IS A NON-SEQUITUR. (a) The chain "more than c 2^m/m^4 pieces ... therefore more than m - 4 log2 m - O(1) Min vertices --- and so 2^{Omega(m)} vertices" does not close: k >= m - 4 log2 m bounds nothing about N, since k Min vertices are k vertices. The 2^{Omega(m)} conclusion is true, but it comes straight from prop:auso-size's own count (N log N >~ 2^m), not from the Min-vertex bound. (b) The Min-vertex bound itself is worthless as a size statement for exactly the reason the route does not state: k Min vertices buy 2^k pieces at a cost of k vertices, so "almost every AUSO needs at least m - O(log m) Min vertices" demands fewer extra vertices than the m Max vertices the game already has. (c) The lower bound A(m) >= A(m-1)^2 by combing one coordinate is folklore in the USO literature (combed USOs are Szabo-Welzl's; the product construction and the resulting counting bound are standard) and carries no attribution; from memory, unchecked against the source, Matousek determined the number of USOs of the n-cube as n^{Theta(2^n)}, which is stronger than 728^{2^{m-3}} = 2^{Theta(2^m)}. Not worth integrating.
findings.evidence: mono.tex, prop:mono-count and its proof; frontier.tex:4166-4200 (prop:auso-size). Arithmetic checked: log2(728)/8 = 1.1885, so 728^{2^{m-3}} = 2^{1.188 * 2^m} — the route's 1.18 is right.

findings.defect: NEW AND CORRECT, BUT SO FAR IT SAYS ONLY WHAT cor:seven-two-player ALREADY SAYS. On every instance the route can evaluate — the two non-Holt-Klee classes at m = 3, the height-7 orientation at m = 4, all ten 4-faces and all forty 3-faces of B^2 — chi_HK is 2, so the bound yields k >= 1, which is exactly "a non-Holt-Klee orientation needs a Min vertex", i.e. cor:seven-two-player. It is not a barrier: it covers none of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi, and the route does not claim otherwise. It is worth keeping as the ONLY instance-specific size lower bound in the realisability programme, and it is now known sharp in exactly one place (B^2, where prop:b2-realised attains k = 1). lem:mono-perturb is sound (dD/deta_{v,1-sigma(v)} = 1 identically, so each zero set is nowhere dense) and is a different device from the paper's lem:tie-perturb (lexicographic perturbation of the objective, attributed to Charnes and to Dantzig-Orden-Wolfe); it should be stated as a lemma about the readout parametrisation, not as a new tie-breaking result.
findings.evidence: mono.tex thm:mono-kbound and lem:mono-perturb; frontier.tex:4319-4338 (cor:seven-two-player), 4955-4993 (lem:tie-perturb); chi4_B2.log, chk.py.

findings.defect: CORRECT AND INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED, BUT IT REFUTES A CLAIM THE PAPER HAD ALREADY WITHDRAWN, AND THE PROPERTY IT TESTS IS CHEAP. I re-derived the m = 3 half from scratch: 728 AUSOs, 18 classes, 168 orientations in 4 classes carry a facet translate, with the route's exact (c,j) pairs and Holt-Klee flags. But (i) the current rem:blowup-realise already says "the realised blow-up of the 2-cube in rem:blowup-measured shows that a game does it by other means at inner dimension two" and already calls the anti-value an obstruction to one substitution, so there is no standing "negative half of the dichotomy" to falsify; (ii) carrying a facet translate is a weak property — 4 of 18 classes at m = 3 — and it is satisfied by the shallowest orientations (the thirteen realised m = 4 witnesses have heights 2, 3 and 4 only, against the height 10 that B^2 needs); (iii) with prop:b2-realised in hand, the whole operation, parity rule and height are realised together, so the isolated ingredient is no longer of interest. At most one sentence, folded into rem:blowup-realise.
findings.evidence: My independent enumeration (audit-mono/tr.py): 728 AUSOs / 18 classes / 168 translates / 4 classes, matching the route exactly. frontier.tex:4843-4905 (rem:blowup-realise as it now stands). trans4_1933_game.json and trans4_11296_game.json re-verified from the game by my own code: stopping, nondegenerate, outmaps as claimed, 4 Max and 0 Min.

findings.defect: GENUINELY NEW AND THE BEST THING IN THE ROUTE — VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. I re-verified both non-Holt-Klee witnesses from the explicit games with my own exact code (greatest trap empty; average part eliminated by exact Gaussian elimination onto C u {t1}; val_sigma as the componentwise minimum over ALL 64 positional Min strategies; outmap read off): X3c_98_game.json is stopping, nondegenerate, 3 Max / 6 Min / 87 avg, outmap (0,1,3,2,5,4,6,7); X3a_170_game.json is stopping, nondegenerate, 3 Max / 6 Min / 159 avg, outmap (0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4). My own USO/acyclicity/Holt-Klee max-flow test confirms both are AUSOs of the 3-cube and both fail Holt-Klee. So two players do realise non-LP orientations at m = 3, and with prop:oneplayer-lp this makes "one-player realisable = Holt-Klee" a THEOREM at m = 3, complementing rem:hk-survey's m = 4 measurement. What the paper currently has is weaker: rem:auso-size says only that the sixteen Holt-Klee classes are "candidates", and rem:auso-census realises just the height-4 class. Worth integrating as one proposition plus the two normal forms.

findings.defect: TRUE, CHEAP, AND NEVER USED. The proof is three lines of concavity and is correct; the "708 incidences, none inside the hull" is a consistency check on a proved theorem, not evidence of anything. It refuted no realisability instance, pruned no search, and is subsumed by rem:mono-iff's LP (it is one family of consequences of the same concave-interpolation feasibility). It is also stated in a needlessly weak form: with one player Psi is affine, so the same argument puts x_sigma outside the AFFINE hull of the opposite face, which is strictly stronger and the route does not say it. Integrate only if it is ever used.

A RE-PRESENTATION OF AN EXISTING GAME, WITH NO IMPROVEMENT. The computation is fine and the conclusion "order (4,2) suffices for the height-7 orbit" is a legitimate small datum. But the route's own gloss — "three Min vertices suffice for it in the construction of thm:mono-iff(b)" — is WORSE than what the paper already has: G# realises that orientation with TWO Min vertices (prop:auso-seven). So the readout construction is lossy in exactly the parameter thm:mono-kbound tries to bound, which is worth saying explicitly (the gap between the lower bound log2 chi_HK = 1 and the constructive upper bound 2m(r-1) = 8 is where any real content would have to live), but the proposition itself adds nothing to the paper.

verdict:
DOES IT MEAN ANYTHING? Partly. One result is worth having, three are already in the paper under other names, one headline is float-only, and the route's central question was answered affirmatively by another route while this one was running.

IS IT NEW? Result by result. lem:mono-readout: its one-player half is verbatim in rem:auso-census ("a one-player game is a family of 2m substochastic affine maps and the orientation is read off an arrangement") and in prop:oneplayer-lp's harmonic normal form; the two-player extension (pin Max, Min survives, so readouts are minima of substochastic affine maps, hence CONCAVE) is new, elementary and correct. thm:mono-iff is round 12's unverified (v4) proved, uncited as such, and it is not an iff as stated (part (a) does not deliver part (b)'s dyadic delta-leaky hypotheses; the rounding lemma is proved only for one player). prop:mono-switchmax is an immediate corollary of thm:peak-law and strictly weaker than it. prop:mono-proj is already asserted in rem:gsharp-bigcube and is Stickney-Watson plus Gaertner-Morris-Ruest plus Hansen & Ibsen-Jensen, all three on this project's standing rediscovery list and all three named in that very remark; the route attributes none of them. prop:mono-count is prop:auso-size in new coordinates (the route says so) plus a folklore combing bound (unattributed) plus a Min-vertex corollary that is weaker than trivial. prop:mono-m3 is genuinely new. prop:mono-translate is new data confirming a point rem:blowup-realise had already conceded. thm:mono-kbound is new but so far says only cor:seven-two-player.

IS IT CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? Not circular: no algorithm, no oracle, nothing target-equivalent is assumed. Not a barrier: thm:mono-kbound and prop:mono-count rule out no algorithm and cover NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6, def:bsi — they belong to the realisability programme, not to sec:gap, and the route does not claim otherwise. No polynomial class is claimed. No lower-bound family is claimed, and none is present: prop:mono-m3's games are single instances at m = 3, not a build(n).

IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? Mostly yes, once. The 18 games of prop:mono-m3 and the 13 of prop:mono-translate are built and checked from the game in exact rationals; I re-verified four of them with independently written code (trap-based stopping, exact elimination of the average part, val_sigma as the componentwise minimum over ALL positional Min strategies, outmap and nondegeneracy) and all four match. The B^2 search failure is correctly calibrated against a known-realisable target and correctly labelled as no evidence — that is exactly the discipline this project asks for. The one lapse is the m = 4 coverage measurement: it is pure numpy with a 1e-9 margin and a silently unconverged Howard loop, no hit is recomputed exactly and no game is built, yet sample.py's docstring asserts "re-verified exactly" and rem:mono-cover4 presents the 44 non-Holt-Klee hits as realisations. That claim is unsupported as it stands.

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it. The route's gap ("is every AUSO realised by a readout system of finite order, and is B^2 realised at order (5,r)?") is soft in both halves: finite order is free, because k Min vertices buy 2^k pieces at a cost of k vertices, and B^2 is realised — prop:b2-realised, 138 vertices, five Max and one Min, i.e. order (5,2). The true gap is the size-faithful one the route's own machinery supports but never states: build.py's Knuth-Yao chain gives N = O(m r D (m+k)) for a dyadic order-(m,r) system of denominator 2^D, so what is missing is a sequence of dyadic delta-leaky readout systems of order (m, r_m) and denominator 2^{D_m} with r_m D_m m = m^{O(1)} whose outmaps have bottom-antipodal height m^{omega(1)} — equivalently, whether the blow-up B of thm:blowup can be iterated at ADDITIVE cost in Min vertices and bits of precision, which is rem:blowup-realise's question verbatim and is now open at the THIRD level, dimension 7 and height 22.

WOULD INTEGRATING THIS MAKE THE PAPER BETTER OR WORSE? As submitted, WORSE: it is a new section built around an open instance that the paper has since closed, it restates thm:peak-law and rem:gsharp-bigcube as new, it presents a float measurement as a family of realisations, and its central theorem is size-blind in a document whose own rem:auso-size has already ruled that size is the whole obstruction. Trimmed to about a fifth, BETTER. Integrate: (1) lem:mono-readout, lem:mono-reduce and thm:mono-iff — but only with the missing rounding lemma supplied so the iff closes, with the size clause N = O(m r D (m+k)) stated in part (b) and the failure of size-faithfulness (r <= 2^k) stated in part (a), and labelled as proving round-12's (v4) and as extending rem:auso-census's one-player normal form; this makes the project's standing search practice a theorem and separates the players cleanly ("one player buys affine readouts, the second buys concavity"). (2) prop:mono-m3, with the two explicit non-Holt-Klee games at N = 98 and N = 170 — I re-verified both; it upgrades rem:auso-size's "candidates" to a theorem at m = 3 and complements rem:hk-survey. (3) thm:mono-kbound as one proposition, with the sentence that it is sharp at B^2 and nowhere else. (4) prop:mono-proj as one paragraph of proof folded into rem:gsharp-bigcube, under that remark's existing attribution. DO NOT integrate: prop:mono-switchmax (thm:peak-law), prop:mono-count (prop:auso-size), prop:mono-hull (true, cheap, unused), prop:mono-gsharp (worse than prop:auso-seven's two Min vertices), rem:mono-cover4 (float-only), rem:mono-gap and the entire B^2 subsection (closed by prop:b2-realised), and prop:mono-translate beyond one sentence in rem:blowup-realise.
